correctness.rationale: For transitive \(R\), \(T(X)\) is successor-closed; hence the iteration from \(T(X)\) ascends. If \(|T(X)|=1\) and the next stage strictly grows, the new point has a nonempty successor set disjoint from \(T(X)\). A terminal SCC in that successor subgraph is at least two worlds or it would lie in \(T(X)\), giving two simultaneous new points and the \(n-1\) cutoff. \(n=1,2\) checked separately. Sharp strict-order and complete-two-world witnesses give exactness. Exhaustive finite checker replayed on 4,180 transitive frames, all 65,328 valuation pairs, sharp chains \(n=3,\ldots,60\). The proof is universal; the checker alone is not.

value.rationale: Iterated knowing-whether on transitive models is a natural semantic finite-model depth invariant, and the exact least universal \(n\)-world cutoff for all \(n\) includes sharp nonreflexive lower bounds and handles all cyclic/transient structures. The terminal SCC lemma explains the sharp exceptional one-point case, improving the immediate cardinality upper bound and giving a useful bound for normalizing consecutive non-contingency blocks in finite K4 reasoning.
